A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DVPO despite the changed title. All 16 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original DVPO training experiments, benchmark scores, computational measurements, held-out comparisons and GVM analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds reward-model comparisons, distribution-shift evaluation and ablations. Some baseline scores are explicitly attributed to external sources, but original results are clearly present.

M1.justification: The TD-trained, trajectory-conditioned GVM and frozen-GVM PPO updates remain. v2 adds a tested preference-only training variant assigning +1/-1 returns to chosen/rejected responses (Appendix G). v1's explicit batch-normalization step disappears from the method description, although tilde-Q remains in the advantage equation; whether implementation also changed is unresolved.

E1.justification: v2 adds RewardBench evaluation across Chat, Chat-Hard, Safety and Reasoning, plus HH-RLHF testing of value models trained on UltraFeedback under distribution shift (Section 6). UltraFeedback and the original MT-Bench, Arena-Hard and AlpacaEval policy evaluations remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds ReMax and GRPO to the Base comparison, PPO and GRPO to the Mistral Instruction comparison, and ReMax/GRPO to computational comparisons. It also directly compares GVM against ScalarRM and the converged PPO critic. The GPT-4 performance row in v1 Table 2 is removed; GPT-4-based judging remains.

E3.justification: v2 extends Instruction optimization to Llama3-8B-Instruct and GVM evaluation to a Llama2-13B configuration. New reward evaluations specify Bellman-style response-level aggregation and evaluation of the PPO critic at convergence. The reported KL coefficient changes from an initial 0.2 to a default 0.05, with a new three-value sweep. These descriptions do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds reward-source ablation comparing scalar rewards with binary preferences, KL sensitivity testing, HH-RLHF distribution-shift analysis, and model-size analysis of GVM accuracy (Section 6 and Appendices E, G and H). The original token-feedback example and GPT-4 judging case studies are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard errors or significance tests. GVM percentile tables summarize token-value aggregation choices, not uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Original Base scores and Mistral DVPO scores are retained, while numerous comparator, reward-evaluation and ablation results are added. Newly reported Llama3-8B-Instruct DVPO scores are 7.72/39.2/42.59 on MT-Bench/Arena-Hard/AlpacaEval2. The instruction baseline's AlpacaEval2 entry changes from 22.92 to 34.38, and reported 3B DVPO convergence changes from 450 to 350 steps. These are reported changes, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v1's equivalence theorem becomes Lemma 3.1 with revised assumptions explicitly bounding both reward-derived and pretrained value estimates. Appendix B expands the advantage-error argument. v2 also adds a convergence corollary asserting PPO-like monotonic improvement, a substantive new guarantee without a separate derivation. The original Bellman conversion argument is retained, not newly introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains policy optimization using a pretrained, frozen GVM. v2 qualifies equivalence as reward pretraining plus value estimation versus direct value pretraining and adds policy-invariance motivation. Headline efficiency claims change from 40% memory and 35% time savings in v1's abstract to 30–40% and 30–45% in v2's introduction.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of Chat versus Chat-Hard performance, critic generalization and distribution-shift robustness, and describes GVM as policy-agnostic despite retaining trajectory conditioning in Section 3.2. New limitations address dataset coverage, bounded approximation error, nonstationarity, unavailable adaptation to fresh feedback and preference-data biases, with periodic GVM refresh proposed as future work.

D1.justification: v2 discloses gamma=1, five GRPO responses per prompt, a scalar linear head and 10K RL prompts, and adds code-access statements and baseline-result provenance. It removes v1's LoRA rank/alpha/dropout specifications and explicit 30%/50% SFT/reward split proportions. These omissions do not establish actual changes to fine-tuning or splitting. Most existing hyperparameters and the judging prompt remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to RewardBench, DAPO and VAPO, explicitly distinguishing DVPO from VAPO's continued actor–critic training. Several earlier background citations disappear, including IPO, SLiC-HF and reward-overoptimization work. The broader positioning against PPO, direct preference optimization and value-guided inference remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, and the experimental setup is reorganized. The proof moves into Appendix B, detailed computational analysis moves into Appendix F, and the conclusion becomes a Discussion section with limitations. New ethics, reproducibility and LLM-use statements further change the document structure.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Figure 1 is redrawn into a two-by-two arrangement, benchmark tables are reorganized by backbone, and six new analysis/ablation tables appear. The training plot changes from two dual-axis panels to four separate panels with revised DVPO step axes. The unchanged held-out win-rate chart moves to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited evidence for replacing reward/critic training: Tables 1–5 and 9–10 add missing baselines, direct GVM comparisons, distribution-shift testing and controlled ablations. Explicit limitations also clarify applicability. These gains substantially strengthen the empirical case, although theoretical and documentation regressions temper the improvement: the new convergence guarantee lacks derivation, Appendix B's constant-gradient assertion conflicts with its policy-dependent equations, and normalization/LoRA details become less explicit.
